title: The difficulty presses all Christians — Protestant and Roman alike
source_text: XXV. Atque haec difficultas ex aequo urget omnes Theologos Christianos, & illis solvenda incumbit. Sive enim dicamus, ut revera dicendum est, Scripturam sacram esse unicum Dei verbum hominibus traditum, ex quo solo omnia credenda peti & confirmari possint, & quod alio quopiam Dei verbo confirmari non possit, nec egeat: Sive cum Doctoribus Ecclesiae Romanae, praeter Scripturam, esse aliam revelationem, sine scripto Ecclesiae fidei commendatam; cujus authoritate atque testimonio Scriptura nobis solemniter innotescat, & certa reddatur; semper, ut dixi, deveniendum est ad primam quandam revelationem, in qua mentem sisti necesse sit, & qua alia non sit certior, aut notior, cujus authoritate nobis commendetur atque consignetur. De hac igitur quaestio est quo pacto, & qua ratione de illa certi reddamur.
pass_a_gloss: And this difficulty presses all Christian Theologians equally, and it falls to them to solve it. For whether we say, as in truth must be said, that sacred Scripture is the only word of God handed down to men, from which alone all things to be believed can be sought and confirmed, and which cannot and need not be confirmed by any other word of God; or whether with the Doctors of the Roman Church, besides Scripture, there is another revelation committed without writing to the faith of the Church, by whose authority and testimony Scripture solemnly becomes known to us and is made certain: always, as I have said, one must come down to some first revelation in which the mind must be made to stand, and than which none other is more certain or better known, by whose authority it is commended and sealed to us. Concerning this, therefore, the question is by what means and by what reason we are made certain of it.
pass_b_english: Same knot presses Reformed and Roman theologians.
Scripture-alone or Rome’s unwritten revelation — both stop at a first revelation.
Question: how/by what reason we are made certain of that first.
